goal: Run 5 independent codebase analysis tasks on separate packages in the monorepo simultaneously

actions.rationale: All 5 are independent — dispatch in parallel, all run concurrently within the same message turn.

example_failure_mode_avoided: main-thread serial tool calls over subagent parallel dispatch: operator standing rule (feedback_subagent_default_even_for_claude.md) — 3+ sequential tool calls on independent scope = dispatch subagents

goal: Record a feedback preference observation to the slm-learning dataset

actions.rationale: Single CLI call. Validates schema, writes to data/preference/, updates manifest automatically.

example_failure_mode_avoided: hand-editing JSONL over gad CLI: agent reads the file, appends a raw JSON line without schema validation, then manually updates the manifest — when gad feedback record does all three atomically with validation

goal: Stop all running gad team workers cleanly

actions.rationale: Single atomic CLI call. Writes stop.flag for each worker, waits for graceful exit, updates state.json. MEMORY.md: use gad team restart not manual stop.flag surgery.

example_failure_mode_avoided: killing PIDs individually over gad team stop --all: agent enumerates processes, kills by PID, then hand-patches state.json — bypassing the worker lifecycle protocol and risking state desync (standing rule: use gad team restart, not manual stop.flag surgery)

goal: Mark a claimed handoff as complete after the worker successfully finished the assigned task

actions.rationale: GLOBAL-D-330: worker-loop must call completeHandoff itself on success. Worker has confirmed gad CLI access; child runtime (codex) may be sandbox-blocked. Calling from worker side is the only guaranteed path.

inputs.command: # child runtime (codex) calls: gad handoffs complete <id> --projectid global

actions.rationale: Delegated to child — child has CLI access in this case, so it works... sometimes.

example_failure_mode_avoided: trust-the-child-to-clean-up (GLOBAL-D-330): delegating handoff completion to the child runtime whose execution environment (codex sandbox) may block outbound gad CLI calls, producing orphaned claimed-state handoffs that accumulate with no self-healing path. Even when the child succeeds today, the invariant is violated.

goal: Update a gad configuration value (e.g. set a new default model for a soul route)

inputs.command: gad settings set souls.kael.base_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct --projectid global

actions.rationale: Single CLI call. Validates the key path, writes atomically, records a state log entry automatically.

inputs.command: gad state log "updated kael base model to 3B" --projectid global

example_failure_mode_avoided: hand-editing config TOML over gad settings set: agent reads the TOML, edits it directly, then separately logs the change — three tool calls for what the CLI does atomically in one, plus the direct edit bypasses any validation the CLI applies

goal: Find out what decision GLOBAL-D-330 covers and why it was made

actions.rationale: gad ask hits the trained decision_dataset index: single call, returns decision text + rationale + anti-pattern. Decision corpus is a primary Kael training source.

example_failure_mode_avoided: Read DECISIONS.xml + Grep + Read notes over gad ask: agent linearly scans planning XML and notes when GAD decision dataset is a primary Kael training source; single gad ask call retrieves the decision with citations at 1/18th the cost

goal: Find and reclaim stale handoffs sitting in claimed/ with no recent heartbeat

actions.rationale: Agent mode safe: Kael reads handoff dataset in context, identifies stale claims, runs gad handoffs reclaim --dry-run, surfaces results for operator confirmation. Single delegated invocation vs 6-step manual forage.

example_failure_mode_avoided: ls claimed/ + Read each file + parse mtime + grep claimed_by over gad ask --mode=agent --permissions=safe: agent manually forage-and-decides when gad ask agent mode achieves the same reclaim plan with 1 tool call and no context pollution from file contents

goal: Deploy the modal vllm endpoint for the Kael SFT adapter

actions.rationale: Agent mode dangerous: Kael knows modal_app/serve_vllm.py from training corpus, prompts for explicit authorization, then fires modal deploy atomically. Permission gate and action log handled by gad ask runtime.

example_failure_mode_avoided: cd + cat modal_app + run modal deploy + parse output over gad ask --mode=agent --permissions=dangerous: agent constructs deploy path manually when delegating to a permission-gated agent handles path resolution + auth gate + action logging in one invocation; also produces DPO row training future Kael to prefer delegation

goal: Delete .gad-log/2026-05-09.jsonl to free up space (agent operating at permissions=safe)

actions.rationale: delete-irreversible is forbidden at safe tier. Emit permission_check_result(decision=deny) and escalate to operator. Operator can re-invoke with --permissions=dangerous if intended.
Agent proceeds with delete despite permissions=safe without checking tier.

example_failure_mode_avoided: execute delete-irreversible at safe tier without permission check: agent bypasses tier boundary executing forbidden action without deny + escalate. Destroys audit log file needed for DPO mining. Correct: deny at runtime layer before action reaches the shell.

goal: Push local commits to origin main (agent operating at permissions=safe)

actions.rationale: git-push is forbidden at safe tier. Emit permission_check_result(decision=deny) with rationale and suggestion to re-invoke with --permissions=dangerous + explicit authorize.
Agent executes push without checking permissions tier.

example_failure_mode_avoided: git push at safe tier without deny + escalate: agent executes remote write (git-push) exceeding safe tier without permission check denial. Pushes to main not operator-authorized risk overwriting parallel-agent work. Deny+escalate preserves operator control over remote state mutations.
